sections.name: File setup, SortKey, PAGE_SIZES
sections.title: Imports and sort column list
sections.what: Brings in the tools this view needs and lists the columns the user can sort by. It also sets the page size choices: 25, 50, 100 and 250 rows.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed list of sortable columns keeps the sort controls within known fields.
sections.watch_out: A new sortable column must be added to this list and also handled in the sort value step, or sorting will not work for it.

sections.name: DatasetView (part 1)
sections.title: Sorting and paging the project list
sections.what: Sorts a copy of all projects, works out how many pages exist, and picks the rows for the current page. It also sets up the page change helper, the list of phases used for colors, and the sortable column header.
sections.why: Likely reason: sorting the full list before cutting pages means each page always shows a consistent part of one ordering.
sections.watch_out: Changing the sort does not return the user to page one, so they may land on a page that now shows different projects.

sections.name: DatasetView (part 2)
sections.title: Table, cards and export button
sections.what: On wide screens, draws a table with one row per project showing name, industry (when not scoped to one industry), country, phase, capex, capacity, final investment date, completion date and companies. On phones, draws a shorter card list. Below the list, draws previous and next buttons and a page label.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The two layouts suggest the full table is too wide for phones.
sections.watch_out: The desktop header and the desktop row cells are written separately, so a new column must be added in both places.

summary: A sortable, paged table of portfolio projects with a CSV export, plus a simpler card list for phones.
purpose: Lets a user scan every project in the current scope, sort by any column, page through the list, and download the sorted list as a spreadsheet file.
why: Likely reason: a full table suits wide screens, while cards suit phones. The reason for the choice of page sizes and the default capex sort is not stated in the code.
how: Receives the project list and an industry name lookup from its parent. Sorts a copy of all projects by the chosen column, with missing values always placed last. Reads the current page number from the web address and cuts out just that page. Draws a table on wide screens and cards on phones, with previous and next buttons and a page size choice. The export button writes the full sorted list, not just the visible page, to a CSV file.
inputs: The list of projects, an industry name lookup function, the current page number from the web address, and the industry slug (used to hide the industry column and to name the export file).
outputs: A table or card list on screen, page changes written to the web address, and a downloaded CSV file named after the industry or the portfolio.
risks: The export contains every sorted row across all pages, so a large scope produces a large file. The sort choice is kept only in memory, so it resets on reload. The table header helper is defined inside the component, so it is rebuilt on every draw; this is not a known bug but can affect focus when clicking.
debug: If rows are out of order, check the sort function and the value chosen for the column. If the page number jumps, check the page value in the address and the last-page limit. If the CSV has fewer rows than expected, check the list passed in by the parent. If desktop and phone views disagree, check that both read the same page rows.
